title: Bigger samples

choices: All three look the same as the population
The size-10 histogram is most accurate
The histograms become symmetric as n grows
The size-10,000 histogram looks most like the population's
explanations: Small samples are bumpy and can miss the long tail.
Fewer values means more chance variation.
The **data** keep the population's skewed shape; it's the distribution of sample **means** that becomes bell-shaped (next lesson).
Correct: large random samples resemble the population.

hints: What does the law of averages say about large n?
Does sampling change the shape of the data?
solution: A large random sample's empirical distribution closely resembles the population distribution, skew and all.
